title: Introduce custodian RBAC sentinel and region-consent proxy
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Introduce a light-weight 'custodian' sentinel that validates operator-scoped claims and enforces region consent before KMS routing. Customers with strict residency requirements sometimes observe requests routed to a fallback provider during capacity pressure; this PR adds a consent gate and a throttled assertion path so operator sessions cannot inadvertently override tenant residency constraints.

Summary of changes: adds a new custodian service (pkg/custodian) that acts as a pre-authorizer for operator-scoped requests; extends rbacv2 decision pipeline with a sentinel hook; augments audit middleware to attach a custody-hash header for post-hoc verification; introduces a region-consent proxy component that annotates KMS routing decisions when tenant consent is present; adds unit, integration, and e2e tests for operator/assertion flows.

Checklist:
- [x] implement custodian sentinel and integrated tests
- [x] extend policy-compiler hooks for operator-scope assertions
- [x] add audit header (X-Redwood-Custody-Hash) and docs
- [x] implement region-consent proxy and KMS affinity tagging
- [x] add feature flag for gradual rollout (feature.custodian.enabled)
- [x] add SLO-preserving throttling when consent validation falls back to async verification

Commits summary: commit 1/6: scaffold custodian service and basic decision interface; commit 2/6: wire sentinel into rbacv2 pipeline and add unit tests; commit 3/6: add audit header producer + signing helper; commit 4/6: implement region-consent proxy and KMS-tag mapping; commit 5/6: add integrational tests (mock KMS, mock policy compiler); commit 6/6: feature flag, config, docs and migrate CI matrix.

Changed areas (high level): pkg/custodian/ (new) - custody decision and claim normalizer; services/rbac/decision_pipeline.go - sentinel hook integration; services/audit/middleware.go - header emission and signer invocation; services/kms/proxy.go - annotate routing decisions with consent tags; integrations/installer/vars.yaml - enablement flag and defaults; docs/security/operator-claims.md - rationale and operational guidance; tests/e2e/operator-consent.test.js - scenario coverage; charts/redwood-helm/templates/custodian-deployment.yaml - k8s manifest and resource requests.

Testing and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e related to the mock KMS race; added deterministic hook and retried. Final CI: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e: pass, lint: pass. Cargo-culted some mocks from pkg/testutil to avoid cross-test interference.

Review conversation (high level):
- Daniel Park: "Can the sentinel be bypassed by elevated operator tokens? Need an explicit denylist if a token has 'operator:override' claim."
  - Author: "Design intentionally treats operator:override as a high-risk claim and requires an explicit enterprise allowlist; added config.operatorOverride.allowlist and unit tests to assert deny by default."
- Sofia Martinez: "Audit header contains base64 signature, but we should avoid leaking raw tenant IDs to downstream telemetry."
  - Author: "Switch to custody-hash (HMAC over request-id + tenant-id) and documented verification steps; telemetry receives only the hash and a minimal audit envelope."
- Jun Li: "What is the performance impact?"
  - Author: "Benchmarks in benchmark-lab showed ~0.6ms median added latency for hot paths when feature flag enabled and async verification turned on; included a throttling policy to eliminate load amplification."
- Reviewer QA thread: "Please add a smoke test that simulates fallback KMS provider and validates consent gate blocks override flows."
  - Author: "Added tests/e2e/operator-consent.test.js scenario 'fallback-no-override' to cover this."
